rooms.name: The Raven's Throat
rooms.desc: A chute of white water between granite walls, boulders the size of carts breaking it into a staircase of foam; spray hangs over every ledge and the roar is everywhere.
rooms.dm: Anyone falling or swept in here takes 2d6 bludgeoning per round among the blocks and is carried 30 ft a round toward the arch; climbing out onto a block or the wall is DC 15 Athletics. No pool: the force does not slacken under the bridge.

rooms.name: The old ford
rooms.desc: A gravel bar under fast, cold water about two feet deep, between two rows of blackened pile stubs. Mud on both banks is churned with tracks.
rooms.dm: Wading is difficult terrain: DC 10 Strength (Athletics) per 10 ft or be swept 10 ft downstream and knocked prone. Off the bar the river is 3-6 ft deep and swimming is DC 13. A DC 12 Survival check on the west-bank mud reads wolf prints and bare human feet together, heading north-west up the old track toward the den west of Lake Baratok (p.32, p.201).

objects.label: Arching stone bridge
objects.desc: A single granite arch over the narrows, humped ten feet above the road, its parapets wet with spray and lined with ravens. A worn raven is carved on the keystone of both faces; moss hangs on the upstream side.

objects.label: The Raven's Throat
objects.desc: White water roaring down a staircase of car-sized granite blocks between the Notch shelves, ten feet of fall in a hundred and fifty with no pool at its foot: standing waves run on under the arch. It never goes quiet.

objects.label: Old piles and the ford
objects.desc: Two rows of blackened timber stubs stand out of the shallows, all that is left of the wooden bridge the stone arch replaced; between them a pale gravel bar where carts used to ford, about two feet deep.

objects.label: Wolf prints and bare feet
objects.desc: Wolf prints and bare human footprints pressed into the mud side by side.
objects.dm: DC 12 Survival: a pack that walks on two legs as often as four, heading north-west up the old track toward the den west of the lake (p.32).

objects.label: Trinket in the mud
objects.desc: Something small glints in the mud between the piles.
objects.dm: Roll on the trinket table in appendix A (p.32).

objects.label: Dire wolf
objects.dm: Day result 12 / night 10: three dire wolves splash across the ford out of the fog on the west bank. The fog lightly obscures the river; the bridge is the party's chokepoint (p.30).

rooms.name: Raven River Crossroads
rooms.desc: Five roads meet on a trampled forest bench beside a river that never stops roaring. A weatherworn signpost leans at the main junction; north-north-west, through a thin screen of tall pines, an arching stone bridge spans the river at a narrows, and behind it white water comes thundering down through a cleft in the rock. A dead, bark-stripped tree full of nests stands over everything, and ravens watch from it, from the signpost and from the stones. Across the road a stone trough and a turnout of crushed granite; east, a milestone where a gravel road climbs south and a dirt path slips north into the pines.
rooms.dm: Always check for a random encounter here (p.40): every 30 minutes outdoors, 18+ on a d20 on the road, 15+ in the woods, no more than two outdoor encounters per 12 hours (p.28); the stagings on this map place each likely result. The rapids impose disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing anywhere on the map. A Keeper of the Feather in raven form always watches from the rookery or the signpost, shadows the party 1d4 hours and flies home to report (p.32). Never harm a raven (p.26): a party that shoots at the rookery is marked and the Keepers will not trust it; a party that leaves the ravens be has the swarms' help in any fight here. Distances from the signpost: Krezk 2 mi west over the bridge (40 min); Vallaki about 4.5 road miles east (1.5 h); Van Richten's Tower about 1.3 mi up the north path (30 min); the winery about 3 mi south-west (1 h; the road becomes a muddy trail after half a mile, then a meadow signpost points west, p.174); Tsolenka gatehouse 7 mi up the gravel road south (2.5-3 h, extreme cold at night, p.157).

objects.label: Signpost
objects.desc: A weatherworn grey-oak fingerpost leaning a little, its cap white with raven droppings and black feathers jammed in its cracks. Krezk points north to the bridge seen through the pines; Vallaki east, up a gentle rise; The Wizard of Wines south-west, gently downhill.

objects.label: Wagon turnout
objects.desc: A hard standing of crushed granite where the wine wagon turns and waits, two sets of wheel ruts arcing through it and hoof-churned mud at its trough end.

objects.label: Stone trough and hitching rail
objects.desc: A long stone watering trough green with slime, fed by a stone spout from a runnel; a hitching rail of two posts and a bar stands between it and the road, the mud round it churned by hooves.

objects.label: Runnel
objects.desc: A stone-lined runnel two feet wide, cut from the river where it comes over the Notch, carries water down the bench to the trough; a granite slab bridges it where the road crosses.

objects.label: The rookery
objects.desc: A dead beech sixty feet tall, its bark stripped to silver-grey wood and its top snapped off, two dozen stick nests crowded in its forks and ravens watching from every limb. The ground beneath is white with droppings and crunches with small bones.

objects.label: Hollow log
objects.desc: A fallen beech trunk, hollow and rotten, lying half under the rookery's limbs with its open end toward the road.

objects.label: Raven stones
objects.desc: A line of five bank boulders under the ravens' flight from the rookery to the bridge, every top capped white; the biggest is a favourite perch.

objects.label: Pine screen
objects.desc: Tall pines with straight bare trunks; from the signpost the bridge's arch shows between them.

objects.label: West knob and the rock ramp
objects.desc: A rounded granite outcrop carrying the bridge's west end, sliced through by a pick-cut road ramp eight feet deep, its walls raked with old tool marks.

objects.label: East knob
objects.desc: A rounded granite outcrop shouldering the bridge's east end and pinching the river against the arch; a small cairn of flat stones stands on its crown.

objects.label: Bridge bollard
objects.desc: A squat granite post with an iron ring, polished by ropes and hooves where wagons are steadied before the hump of the bridge.

objects.label: The Notch
objects.desc: Two wet granite shelves twelve feet high flank the river where it comes through a cleft in the low lip north of the crossroads; lake fog slides over them in slow sheets. A worn ledge path runs along the top of the eastern one.

objects.label: League stone
objects.desc: A squat, waist-high milestone of the old roads, its numerals worn shallow and a sun sigil cut above them; lichen hides half of it. It marks the branch to the pass.

objects.label: Tsolenka road boulders
objects.desc: Two car-sized boulders flank the gravel road where it starts to climb toward the pass; old grey snow crusts the lee of the northern one and rime whitens the gravel even in summer.

objects.label: Trail cairn
objects.desc: A knee-high cairn of stacked flat stones, the first marker of the pass road.

objects.label: Torn corpse
objects.desc: A man in muddy homespun lies in the ditch beside the path, torn apart by something with very big jaws; huge paw prints are pressed into the mud all round him.

objects.label: Robbed grave
objects.desc: Beside the road a shallow grave has been dug open and left: a mud-filled hole, the spoil and the stones that covered it thrown about, bones and a scrap of rusted mail in the dirt.

objects.label: Encounter check on arrival (p.40). Day table result 11 (ravens or wereraven), 16 (werewolves posing as trappers on the bridge), 12 (dire wolves at the ford), 2 (scouts by the tower path), 19 (scarecrows up the winery trail), 8 (skeletal rider on the bridge), 7 (Vistani at the trough); see the hidden figures for each.

The river: 30 ft wide at the narrows, 45 ft at the piles, 3-6 ft deep and fast. Ford: difficult terrain, DC 10 Athletics per 10 ft or swept 10 ft downstream and prone. Swimming elsewhere DC 13. Swept into the Throat: 2d6 bludgeoning per round. A fall from the deck is 16 ft into water (1d6).

The east shelf: DC 12 Athletics to climb the wet rock from the bench (the cut steps at its south end are an easy scramble). Its ledge path skirts the crossroads above the bridge, unseen and unheard over the rapids; it overlooks the bridge deck.

The old track up from the ford, grassing over: wolf prints and bare feet lead north-west toward the werewolf den in the caves west of Lake Baratok, about 1.7 mi (p.32, p.201). Kiril Stoyanovich's pack haunts these woods (p.171).
West: the Old Svalich Road to Krezk (S), 2 miles; past Krezk it runs a little over a mile more into the Mists (p.143).
East: the Old Svalich Road climbs gently to Vallaki (N), about 4.5 road miles.
North-north-east: the dirt path to Van Richten's Tower on Lake Baratok (V), about 1.3 miles; its right fork is the long dirt trail that rejoins the road at the Luna River crossroads (p.40).
South: the gravel Tsolenka Pass road (T), 7 miles to the gatehouse; wind, snow and bitter night cold on the climb (p.157).
South-west: the winery road dips south and becomes a gravel trail; the Wizard of Wines (W) is about 3 miles on (p.174).

Wine Delivery (p.180): once the winery is freed, Adrian and Elvir Martikov bring three barrels this way to Vallaki or Krezk, watering at the trough. Check for an encounter each mile; two swarms of ravens guard the wagon. Krezk depends on these deliveries (p.143).
Wereraven's bundle
objects.desc: A leather-wrapped bundle of drab clothes stuffed into the hollow end of the log.
objects.dm: Left by the Keeper of the Feather on watch in the rookery, who changes back here (Hidden Bundle, p.30). Taking it strands the Keeper in raven form until it is returned; returning it unasked earns its trust.

objects.label: Keepers' feather mark
objects.desc: A small feather scratched into the underside of the Krezk arm.
objects.dm: The mark of the Keepers of the Feather: this crossroads is watched. A Keeper warms to a party that mentions it (p.40, p.32).

objects.label: Corroded dagger in the spoil
objects.desc: A dagger eaten by rust, half buried in the thrown earth.
objects.dm: The robbers missed it: DC 10 Investigation in the spoil. The grave was a soldier's; the bones and mail scrap lie in the open. The book's intact version is a rocky cairn (p.30); this one is violated, and the Vistani at the trough have its earth on their spades.

objects.label: Corpse's pockets
objects.desc: A wine-chit stamped with a Krezk mark and a carved wooden holy symbol.
objects.dm: The missing villager the Barovian scouts are hunting for (p.29-30). The prints round him are dire-wolf sized and lead to the ford.

objects.label: Keeper's cache under the cairn
objects.desc: Under the cairn's loose top stone: a dozen black feathers bound together and a stub of charcoal.
objects.dm: DC 13 Perception notices the loose top stone. The Keepers use the charcoal to mark signposts; the feathers are tokens for allies.

objects.label: Swarm of ravens
objects.dm: Day result 11 (50%), or whenever the party lingers: the swarms lift from the rookery and circle. They fly off if attacked; otherwise they watch over the party and join any fight here against hostile creatures (p.32).

objects.label: Keeper of the Feather (wereraven, raven form)
objects.dm: Always present as the Keepers' lookout: on the signpost cap, a bollard or the parapet, and back to the rookery if stared at. Stealth against passive Perception; it shadows the party 1d4 hours, then flies home to report (the winery or the Blue Water Inn). On a second meeting it invites them to the Blue Water Inn (p.32).

objects.label: Barovian scout
objects.playerLabel: A hooded figure with a crossbow
objects.dm: Day result 2: three scouts crouched in the pines with crossbows levelled; passive Perception 16 to spot them. They lower their weapons and ask for help finding a missing villager, then recognise the man in the ditch (p.29-30).

objects.label: Barovian scout
objects.playerLabel: A hooded figure with a crossbow

objects.label: Barovian scout
objects.playerLabel: A hooded figure with a crossbow

objects.label: Scarecrow (raven-killer)
objects.dm: Day result 19 / night 17: Baba Lysaga's scarecrows, dead ravens stuffed in their guts, lurching up the winery trail toward the rookery; the ravens shriek and scatter. Surprise unless passive Perception 11 (p.31).

objects.label: Vistani bandit
objects.dm: Day result 7: four grave-robbers lounging round the trough, pipe smoke and laughter in the fog, muddy spades from the grave by the Krezk road. Not hostile unless provoked; they offer to guide for 100 gp, and one carries 2d4 gems (p.32).

objects.label: Martikov wine wagon
objects.desc: An open farm wagon with three wine barrels roped on its bed.
objects.dm: The Wine Delivery after the winery is freed (p.180): coming up the winery road, watering at the trough, then east to Vallaki or over the bridge to Krezk.

objects.label: Adrian Martikov (wereraven, stand-in figure)
objects.dm: Adrian drives; Elvir walks beside. Both are wereravens of the Keepers (p.180). Their two raven swarms attack anything that threatens the wagon.

rooms.name: The bridge crown
rooms.desc: The level crown of the arch, fifteen feet wide between waist-high parapets, sixteen feet above the white water; the stones are slick with spray and the roar drowns speech. Ravens line the parapets. Upstream the Throat pours down at you; downstream the river slides away past the black stubs of an older bridge.
rooms.dm: No cover but the parapets; nobody on the deck can hear anyone coming. A creature shoved over the parapet falls 16 ft into the water (1d6 bludgeoning) and is in the current. The bridge is the chokepoint for the dire wolves at the ford and the place the werewolf trappers choose to hail travellers.

objects.label: Werewolf posing as a trapper
objects.dm: Day result 16: three werewolves in human form, posing as trappers, come over the bridge from the Krezk side. This one hails the party from the crown and asks about silvered weapons; with none in sight they attack in hybrid form. Night result 15 is the pack in wolf form, howling from the Notch and following to strike at the next rest (p.32).

objects.label: Skeletal rider
objects.dm: Day and night result 8: a skeleton on a skeletal warhorse crosses the deck east to west, rusted lantern raised and shedding no light. It ignores the party unless attacked (p.31). Stand-in stats: skeleton and warhorse skeleton.

rooms.name: East shelf and ledge path
rooms.desc: A flat top of wet granite twelve feet above the bench, lichen and puddles on it, the Throat roaring below its sheer western face. A worn path runs along the brink, and at its south end the shelf looks straight down onto the bridge deck. Fog from the lake slides over it.
rooms.dm: The ledge path lets anyone skirt the crossroads above the bridge unseen; nothing on it can be heard over the rapids. Wereravens and werewolves both use it. Climbing up from the bench is DC 12 Strength (Athletics) except by the rough steps at the south end. The werewolf pack howls from here at night (result 15).

rooms.name: West shelf
rooms.desc: A wet granite shelf on the far side of the Throat, its eastern face dropping sheer into the white water; stunted pines cling to its back.
rooms.dm: Reached from the Krezk road side by a DC 12 Athletics scramble. From here a watcher sees the bridge, the east bank and the rookery across the rapids.

objects.label: Scuffs on the ledge path
objects.desc: Claw scrapes and boot scuffs in the green slime along the brink.
objects.dm: Wereravens and werewolves both use this path to skirt the crossroads; fresh scrapes mean the pack passed within the day.

objects.label: Werewolf posing as a trapper
objects.dm: Within whistling distance of the one on the bridge, on the ledge path above the Throat.

objects.label: Swarm of bats (Strahd's spy)
objects.dm: Night result 9, or the dusk and dawn spy check (p.29): bats pour out of the Notch at dusk and over the bridge. The spy's goal is to escape with a report or snatch an item.
